findings.reason: The diff replaces the isRecord(collection) ? collection : ... branch with an unconditional collection.constructor(iters[0]). The RecordType factory at src/Record.js:56-57 returns a new instance, so the locked test at __tests__/issues.ts:131-136 (expect(emptyRecord.merge({id:1})).toBe(emptyRecord)) now fails. For class subclasses (supported, e.g. __tests__/RecordJS.js:35), calling the class constructor without new throws. Both reviewers describe this same removed guard, so I merged their findings and kept the severity at high.
findings.claim: The change removes the isRecord guard, so merging a non-empty value into an empty Record no longer returns the same instance. It now calls collection.constructor(iters[0]), which builds a new record (plain factory) or throws a TypeError (ES class subclass).
findings.evidence: The diff swaps `return isRecord(collection) ? collection // Record is empty and will not be updated: return the same instance : collection.constructor(iters[0]);` for an unconditional `return collection.constructor(iters[0]);` and removes the isRecord import. For `Record({})()`, `toSeq().size === 0`, there is no `__ownerID`, and there is one non-empty iter, so this branch runs. RecordType(values) at src/Record.js:52-97 then returns `new RecordType(values)`, which is a different object. In it, `l.set(this._indices[k], ...)` runs with `_indices['id'] === undefined`. The locked test at __tests__/issues.ts:131-136 (`Issue #1785`) asserts `expect(emptyRecord.merge({ id: 1 })).toBe(emptyRecord)`, which needs identity, so this pass-to-pass test now fails. No story or acceptance text in the packet asks for this behaviour to change.
